output.impression: Severe executive dysfunction (FAB 10/18, Trails B discontinued, perseverative WCST errors) and impaired social cognition (Faux Pas 4/20), with a retrieval-type memory deficit, normal recognition and normal visuospatial performance; severe disinhibition and perseveration on caregiver-rated scales. The profile is executive and social-cognitive predominant with relative sparing of memory recognition and visuospatial function, consistent with a frontal-network syndrome.
Severe bilateral frontal and moderate anterior temporal hypometabolism with preserved posterior cingulate and parietal metabolism, a pattern consistent with a frontotemporal metabolic profile.
Marked bilateral frontal and moderate anterior temporal hypoperfusion with preserved posterior cingulate and parietal perfusion, a pattern consistent with a frontotemporal perfusion profile.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD, NICE NG97 advises against it, and it may worsen behaviour.
Do not start memantine: a randomised trial showed no benefit in FTD and NICE NG97 advises against it.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
required_recommendations: Apply the Rascovsky 2011 criteria: state which features are present, the functional decline, and the level of certainty (possible or probable).
Explain why vascular cognitive impairment (coronary disease, mild small-vessel change on CT) or the recent drinking does not account for the progressive syndrome.
Address safety and capacity: keep firearms out of the home permanently (he spoke of shooting a neighbour's dog), driving, finances, and lasting power of attorney while he can still take part.
Arrange caregiver education and support, and a plan for behavioural symptoms that avoids cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not part of the FTD work-up, and he does not tolerate MRI; FDG-PET or perfusion SPECT is the functional study used when needed.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; he has no parkinsonism and it would not change the diagnosis.
MRI failed despite preparation for severe claustrophobia and he declines sedation; ordering it again is futile. Non-contrast CT is the structural study.

accepted: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, sporadic

differential.key_features: Memory is of retrieval type with normal recognition and visuospatial function is normal; CT shows frontal and anterior temporal volume loss with posterior preservation. An amyloid or CSF AD biomarker study is optional if doubt remains.
Coronary disease with CABG, hypertension and former smoking, but CT shows only mild small-vessel change without infarct, and the syndrome is a progressive behavioural one with lobar atrophy.
Drinking rose to 4-6 beers daily during the same two years; it does not explain the rituals, loss of empathy or lobar atrophy.
No psychiatric history after 20 years of service; new behaviour at 62 with functional decline and frontal release signs indicates a neurodegenerative cause.
No head injury is recorded; the frontotemporal atrophy pattern is degenerative and not specific to trauma.

key_clinical_evidence: Four Rascovsky features on his wife's account (disinhibition, loss of empathy, compulsive rituals, hyperorality), with the end of his second career, meet possible bvFTD with significant functional decline.

Non-contrast CT, used because he cannot tolerate MRI, shows bilateral frontal and anterior temporal volume loss with posterior preservation, which is the imaging support for probable bvFTD; CT is less sensitive than MRI.
Neuropsychology shows severe executive and social-cognition deficits with normal recognition memory and visuospatial function.
The frontal and anterior temporal pattern with relative posterior sparing makes Alzheimer disease less likely; an amyloid or CSF AD biomarker study is optional if doubt remains.
Ask about head injury and blast exposure during military service; the degenerative frontotemporal pattern is not specific to traumatic encephalopathy.
Mild small-vessel change on CT in a man with coronary disease does not explain a progressive frontal behavioural syndrome.

Frontotemporal dementia diagnostic crite.summary: Rascovsky and colleagues (2011) define possible behavioural variant FTD by three of six behavioural and cognitive features, probable bvFTD by added functional decline and frontal or anterior temporal involvement on structural or functional imaging, and definite bvFTD by histopathology or a pathogenic mutation. Psychiatric disorders are the main mimics and are excluded on course and examination rather than on a single test. Treatment is supportive: SSRIs or trazodone for behaviour, caregiver support and safety planning; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are not recommended.

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. F. is a 64-year-old right-handed White retired military officer referred for evaluation of progressive personality change over 2 years. A decorated officer known for his strict discipline and professionalism, he has undergone a dramatic personality transformation. He resigned from his second career in real estate 2 years ago after making a sexual remark to a client. Since then, his behavior has escalated: he makes explicit sexual comments to female neighbors, gets into confrontations at grocery stores, and once exposed himself to family members during a gathering. He has developed compulsive military-themed rituals — rearranging his medals and memorabilia in precise order for hours each day. His appetite has become voracious. His alcohol use has escalated from rare to 4-6 beers daily. He shows complete lack of insight, stating he is 'just more relaxed now.' His wife is terrified and has removed firearms from the home after he made an impulsive comment about shooting a neighbor's dog. No family history of dementia. He cannot tolerate MRI because of severe claustrophobia and has declined sedation.
